@Halio1984 @BillyM2k @kevinolearytv Dogecoin works alright now that almost nobody is using it, but as designed, if everyone used it, the blockchain would quickly grow in size 10x faster than the Bitcoin blockchain.

To scale on L1, you would need more bandwidth and power, and would need to use a datacenter server.

@Halio1984 @BillyM2k @kevinolearytv You need to assume that the 1MB blocks will be full every 1 minute for Dogecoin (every 10 minutes for Bitcoin). After 13 years of continuous nearly full block utilization the Bitcoin blockchain is <500 GB, which fits into a standard hard drive. Dogecoin would be 10x this size.

@AlexLon74173321 @RoninImperial @RichDevX @BillyM2k @kevinolearytv It's pretty obvious if you just do the math.
Bitcoin blockchain size is <500 GB after 13 years of continuous operation.
Since Dogecoin uses 1 minute blocks instead of 10 minute blocks, the Dogecoin blockchain would be 5 TB (10x) after 13 years of continuous use.
Most HDs are ~1TB

@RichDevX @AlexLon74173321 @occupymars42069 @RoninImperial @BillyM2k @kevinolearytv I think most people who are using Dogecoin don't realize that Dogecoin would become completely centralized and insecure if people actually started using Dogecoin at the capacity it is designed for (filling 1 MB blocks every 1 minute). Bitcoin fixes that flaw with 10 minute blocks

@RichDevX @AlexLon74173321 @occupymars42069 @RoninImperial @BillyM2k @kevinolearytv My point is comparing the decentralization and security of each blockchain. If you want to be be sure that your money won't get lost, that the currency supply won't increase, and that the network remains secure and decentralized; you want to store money in Bitcoin, not Dogecoin.

@AlexLon74173321 @occupymars42069 @RichDevX @RoninImperial @BillyM2k @kevinolearytv Dogecoin's blockchain is tiny because nobody uses it. If people actually used Dogecoin, its 1 MB blocks would actually get filled every 1 minute, and the Dogecoin blockchain would be 10x as large as Bitcoin, or ~5 TB instead of Bitcoin's <500 GB.

People use Bitcoin, not Dogecoin

@occupymars42069 @RichDevX @RoninImperial @BillyM2k @kevinolearytv Yes. Disk space grows at the speed of Moore's Law, meaning that it doubles every 24 months.
After 13 years Bitcoin takes less than 500 GB of diskspace. Let's say Dogecoin grows 10x faster due to 1 minute blocks instead of 10 minute blocks. Dogecoin would take up ~5TB in 13 years.
